The BOLD Act’s bipartisan support shows Washington’s addiction to throwing money at symptoms, not solutions. Real progress requires redirecting funds from bloated bureaucracies to actual cures—like accelerating FDA approvals for breakthrough therapies and slashing red tape that delays treatments. 

Every dollar wasted on redundant programs is a dollar not spent on research that could end Alzheimer’s. The administration’s focus on efficiency isn’t “cruel”—it’s about cutting through D.C.’s performative spending to prioritize results.
